title: Delaware's high school football tradition returns to Delaware Stadium with a bigger purpose than the final score. - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Writer ,
6 hours ago Tickets still available for the 70th Blue-Gold game Thursday night Tickets are still available for Thursday night’s 70th DFRC Blue-Gold All-Star Football Game, giving families, alumni, and supporters of Delawareans with intellectual disabilities one more chance to take part in one of the state’s longest-running sports traditions.
The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Thursday, June 18, at Delaware Stadium at the University of Delaware in Newark. Parking opens at 3 p.m., stadium gates open at 5 p.m. and opening ceremonies begin at 6 p.m.
The annual game brings together some of Delaware’s top high school seniors for their final football showcase. But Blue-Gold has always been more than an all-star game. It is DFRC’s signature fundraiser and a statewide celebration of inclusion, leadership and community.
A Father-Son Tradition For fathers looking for a summer night out with young athletes, the game offers something different from watching football on television. The players on the field are Delaware high school seniors, close enough in age that younger boys and girls can imagine themselves someday wearing a high school jersey, running onto a field and representing their school.
It is also a manageable “first big game” experience for young fans: a college stadium, bands, cheerleaders, football under the lights and a crowd filled with families, classmates and local supporters.
For parents, that makes the night both fun and useful. The game gives dads and moms a chance to talk with their children about effort, sportsmanship, service and what it means to use athletic talent to support something larger than yourself.
That larger purpose is what brings many supporters back year after year. The DFRC Blue-Gold program supports Delawareans with intellectual disabilities and highlights the abilities, friendships and dignity of the people the organization serves. The Hand-in-Hand Program, a central part of the Blue-Gold tradition, pairs high school participants with children and young adults with intellectual disabilities, creating friendships that are celebrated throughout the spring and on game night.
For families, volunteers, educators, advocates and disability community supporters, Thursday’s game is a chance to see inclusion in action. The pageantry around the game, including the parade and opening ceremonies, helps make the night feel less like a fundraiser and more like a statewide community reunion.
The night also carries special meaning for Blue-Gold alumni. For former players, cheerleaders, band members, ambassadors and volunteers, returning to the game is a way to reconnect with a defining Delaware experience. Many alumni remember the game not only for football, but for the Buddy Program, the friendships they formed and the lesson that leadership is measured by how people treat others.
The 70th game adds to that sense of history. Alumni can watch a new class of seniors step into the same tradition they once carried, while families can introduce younger children to an event that has been part of Delaware’s sports and civic life since 1956.
Blue will be the home team and Gold will be the visiting team.
Tickets are available through the University of Delaware’s event system, with general admission and reserved seating options. Tickets also may be available at the UD ticket window on game day.
To Go What: 70th DFRC Blue-Gold All-Star Football Game When: Thursday, June 18 Where: Delaware Stadium, University of Delaware, Newark Schedule: Parking opens at 3 p.m.; stadium gates open at 5 p.m.; opening ceremonies begin at 6 p.m.; kickoff is 7 p.m. Teams: Blue is the home team; Gold is the visiting team. Tickets: Available through the University of Delaware event system. Additional fees may apply. Why go: To watch Delaware high school seniors compete, support DFRC’s work with Delawareans with intellectual disabilities, celebrate the Hand-in-Hand Program and take part in one of Delaware’s longest-running sports traditions.
